These are string literals in a signed, persisted sidecar payload — the exact byte sequence is the contract, not intent
findings.finding: The leaf defines the `tier` field's enumerated values as `first_class` and `best_effort` (underscores), but the parent epic's acceptance criterion worked example explicitly specifies the string `best-effort` (hyphen): "the run's provenance records tier `best-effort`". These are non-identical string literals for the same field in a signed, persisted payload — a consumer following the parent's worked example who checks `tier == 'best-effort'` will never match a leaf that writes `'best_effort'`. Under the conflict rule the parent wins; the leaf redefines a parent deliverable differently.
findings.location: Leaf Approach section ('`tier` is `first_class` or `best_effort`') vs. Parent epic AC worked example ('the run's provenance records tier `best-effort`')
scenarios: A consumer reads the parent epic's worked example, writes `assert verdict['provider_provenance']['tier'] == 'best-effort'`, and the check silently fails because the leaf produces `'best_effort'`

The parent epic's plan-review attestation was signed against the `best-effort` form; if the leaf ships `best_effort`, the parent's attested AC is materially inconsistent with the delivered artifact, forcing a re-attestation of the parent
findings.suggested_fix: Change the leaf's Approach to read: "`tier` is `first-class` or `best-effort`" (hyphens), matching the parent epic's worked example. findings.finding: The plan does not specify how provenance data flows from the `ProviderSession` builder back to `runner.run()`. `provider_factory` is a `(str) -> Provider` hook passed to pydantic-ai's `infer_model` — it can only return a `Provider` object, not metadata. The plan says `providers.py` will 'expose the provenance record from the factory' and `runner.py` will 'populate it alongside `ran_model`' but leaves the actual API shape unspecified (e.g. session side-effect attribute, a second method, a wrapper return type). Additionally, for the 'lazy-string' branch (lines 301–306 in runner.py where `is_resolvable` but not `supports` — e.g. bare `openai:gpt-4o` without `base_url`) no builder is called through the session at all, so there is no provenance side-effect to read; the plan does not address what `provider_provenance` should contain in this case.
findings.location: Scope section: 'src/rebar/llm/providers.py — expose the provenance record from the factory' and 'src/rebar/llm/runner.py — populate it alongside ran_model'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `ProviderSession.last_provenance: ProviderProvenance | None` attribute, set by each builder as a side-effect (including `_build_openai` when `base_url` is set). For the lazy-string path, construct provenance in `runner.run()` from the resolved provider-name string and `cfg.base_url` (yielding tier='unknown' or omitting the field). Document both paths explicitly in the Scope section.

findings.finding: The plan assigns new implementation work to `providers.py` ('expose the provenance record from the factory') but the file self-reports as already at 289/300 LOC at its last significant edit (line 219 comment), and S4 subsequently added the `_build_openai` method bringing the file to 299 lines (verified by reading to EOF). Any non-trivial addition to this file would breach the 300-LOC cap that was attested by a closed story (S1 / 7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1), exactly the constraint S2 named when routing capability code to `capabilities.py` instead. An implementer treats `tier` as `'first_class' if provider in {'anthropic', 'bedrock'} else 'best_effort'`, which differs from the base_url-based rule implied by the test — and the two rules disagree on an Anthropic run going through a local proxy (base_url set, provider='anthropic').

findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Scope section's `capabilities.py` spec: 'The `tier` field is derived by the following rule (applied in order): (1) if `base_url is not None` → `"best_effort"`, regardless of provider; (2) if `provider in {"anthropic", "bedrock"}` → `"first_class"`; (3) else → `"best_effort"`. Plan Approach: 'cfg.base_url the endpoint'
providers.py:209: direct = _local_proxy_bypass_base_url() — this may REPLACE cfg.base_url with the upstream Anthropic API URL

findings.finding: For the Anthropic provider, the effective endpoint is not cfg.base_url but the result of _local_proxy_bypass_base_url(), which replaces a loopback cfg.base_url with the direct Anthropic API URL. The plan specifies the assembler takes cfg.base_url as the endpoint primitive (Scope section), but this produces a wrong endpoint_host for any run where the loopback-bypass logic fired — the stamped host would be the operator-configured loopback, not the actual API host contacted.
findings.location: Scope section ('cfg.base_url the endpoint') and Approach section ('cfg.base_url the endpoint'); providers.py:_build_anthropic() lines 209-212
scenarios: Operator has ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set to a loopback address (e.g. Claude Code proxy on 127.0.0.1); rebar bypasses it and hits api.anthropic.com, but endpoint_host stamps the loopback address from cfg.base_url.
Even without a loopback, cfg.base_url for Anthropic is typically None (the SDK default), so the stamped endpoint_host would be None rather than 'api.anthropic.com'.
